Location: Pascagoula Anchorage, Gulf side of Horn Island / Petit Bois Island (30°05.5'N 88°25.0'W)
Item: Coast Guard safety zone – 1,000 m around tanker KALAHARI at Pascagoula Anchorage, through Dec 27
Details: The Coast Guard has set a temporary safety zone covering all water within 1,000 meters (about 0.6 mile) of the tanker M/T KALAHARI while she does repairs at anchor in the Pascagoula Anchorage (notice 26-134). No vessel may enter without permission. Why it matters: boats running the outside route along the Mississippi barrier islands, or heading in and out of Horn Island Pass, need to steer around a ship-sized no-go circle for the next two months – easy to miss at night.
When: Oct 28 2026, 6am – Dec 27 2026, 6pm CDT (enforced while the tanker is anchored there)
Notes: What to do: plot the circle (center 30°05.533'N, 088°24.958'W, radius 1,000 m) before you go; to ask permission to enter, call COTP Mobile on VHF 16 or (251) 266-5888. Waterways Management: (251) 382-8653. Zone ends early if the tanker leaves the anchorage. Map point is the zone center.

Location: Bayou Sorrel swing bridge (LA 75), GIWW Port Allen–Morgan City Alternate Route, about mile 38.3
Item: UPDATE: Bayou Sorrel swing bridge – full repair closures set for Dec 8, 10, 13 and Jan 19, 21
Details: The damaged Bayou Sorrel swing bridge (in the sheet since Oct 20, opening for boats only in set daily windows) now has full repair closures scheduled: Dec 8 8:30am–4:30pm, Dec 10 6am–5pm, Dec 13 8:30am–4:30pm, Jan 19 8:30am–4:30pm and Jan 21 8:30am–4:30pm. Why it matters: if your mast needs the bridge to swing, you won't get through the Alternate Route on those days – plan the Port Allen–Morgan City leg around them or go the main GIWW via the Harvey/Algiers locks.
Notes: What to do: call the bridge on VHF before arriving and avoid the closure days; the Bayou Sorrel Lock is at (225) 659-2581 if you need local status. Uncertain: these dates come from American Commercial Barge Line's river report only – no Coast Guard or DOTD notice found yet. Harvey Lock was reported closed again since Oct 22 (reverse head) in the same report, so check both routes. Map point is approximate.

Location: Homosassa – Civic Club Festival Grounds, 5530 S Mason Creek Rd (Homosassa River, Nature Coast)
Item: Homosassa Arts, Crafts and Seafood Fest
Details: Nature Coast seafood weekend – stone crab, grouper, shrimp, gumbo, chowder and lobster rolls, plus arts and crafts. Hours Sat 9am–5pm, Sun 9am–4pm. Why it matters: a good excuse to poke up the Homosassa River – stone crab season is on.
Notes: What to do: the Homosassa River is shallow and winding – check depth for your draft and the tide before you go upriver. Dates and venue are from a festival calendar; confirm with the organizer. Same weekend as the Fort Myers Boat Show, Jubilee Regatta and Penfield Flying Scot Regatta.

Location: Yankeetown – Riverside Drive on the Lower Withlacoochee River, about 3 miles from the Gulf
Item: Yankeetown Arts, Crafts and Seafood Festival
Details: Old-Florida riverside festival the weekend before Thanksgiving: locally caught Gulf seafood, entertainment, arts and crafts. Free admission and parking; Sat 9am–5pm, Sun 9am–4pm. Why it matters: one of the few festivals you can almost reach by boat on this quiet stretch of the Big Bend coast.
Notes: What to do: the Withlacoochee channel is shallow – check charts and tide for your draft. Dates are from a festival calendar; confirm with the organizer. Same weekend as the Egmont Key Race and the Ormond Beach Riverfest (whose venue the same calendar now gives as Rockefeller Gardens and Fortunato Park, by the Granada Blvd bridge).

Location: St. Augustine bayfront and historic downtown (Matanzas River / Atlantic ICW, Bridge of Lions)
Item: Nights of Lights – about 3 million lights, opening with Light-Up! Night Nov 21
Details: St. Augustine's holiday lights festival (since 1993) runs Nov 21, 2026 – Jan 18, 2027. Light-Up! Night on Sat Nov 21 starts with music at 4pm in the Plaza de la Constitución. Why it matters: the bayfront and Bridge of Lions light up right on the ICW – a classic stop for southbound snowbirds, and moorings and slips fill fast.
When: Nov 21 2026 – Jan 18 2027; Light-Up! Night Sat Nov 21 from 4pm
Notes: What to do: reserve a mooring or slip early for Nov 21 and the holiday weekends; the Bridge of Lions will be busy with tour boats in the evenings. Sources differ on the last day (Sun vs Mon Jan 18) – the date is Jan 18 either way. Same night as the Ormond Beach Riverfest and Yankeetown festival weekend.
